subject: Vendr onboarding: evidence embargo & manifest
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@vendr.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendr onboarding: evidence embargo & manifest

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the onboarding kickoff last week. Before we start pushing artifacts into the Vendr portal, we have a couple of operational constraints on our side and wanted to confirm vendor-side capabilities so we can avoid repeated re-uploads. High level ask: we need to stage evidence under a short embargo (private visibility) until our security team performs an initial review, then flip visibility to the review group in Vendr.

Specifically:
- Can Vendr accept S3 presigned uploads where objects are private until we request release?
- Is there a way for you to set an upload TTL (we’d like 7 days for temporary staging) or at minimum 72 hours?
- We’ll provide a CSV manifest that contains object keys, CAIQ/SIG mapping, and SOC 2 artifact tags — does Vendr support bulk manifest ingestion or do we need to attach per-question artifacts?
- Any constraints on filename patterns or max file size we should know about?

Attached is a lightweight manifest template (evidence-manifest-template.csv) and a short doc with our suggested field mapping. Suggested schedule: if we can confirm upload mechanism today, we’ll prepare a compact set (~12 artifacts) and request a staged upload window on Wed 5/19 so security can review before end of week.

Let me know what you can support and any requirements you have from the Vendr side. If helpful we can do a 20-minute screen-share to walk through the manifest.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: evidence-manifest-template.csv (CSV template), vendr-upload-instructions.pdf (shortops)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@vendr.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Vendr onboarding: evidence embargo & manifest

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear note and the manifest sample — that’s really helpful. Quick answers below and then a proposed approach.

1) S3 presigned uploads: yes, we support presigned PUTs to an ephemeral ingest bucket. Files uploaded via presigned URL are private by default in our pipeline.

2) TTL: we can set object lifecycle rules on the ingest bucket. Standard options are 72 hours or 7 days; we can do 7 days if you prefer (we’d configure a temp TTL on our side and can surface an "expand" button to extend on request).

3) Manifest ingestion: Vendr supports CSV manifests for bulk attach. Required columns: filename, object_key, question_id (or CAIQ/SIG mapping tag), evidence_type, created_at. Your template looks close — we’ll validate during ingest and return a small report listing any missing mappings.

4) Limits: max single file 250 MB; filenames should avoid Unicode control characters; recommended pattern: <customer>_<artifact>_<YYYYMMDD>.<ext>.

Proposed flow:
- You provide completed manifest (CSV) + presign request (list of object_keys).
- We return presigned URLs for each key (7-day TTL by default).
- You upload artifacts into presigned URLs. Objects remain private until a Redwood reviewer clicks "release to Vendr reviewers" in our portal.

Security note: we can also add an S3 server-side encryption header (AES-256) during presign if you want.

I can generate a presign batch today if you attach the manifest. I’ll also attach a one-page upload guide.

Best —
Elena Ruiz
Vendor Integration Lead, Vendr
elena@vendr.com

Elena —

Thanks, that flow works for us. A couple of clarifications/asks before you generate presigns: 

- Please use the 7-day TTL on presigns. Our preferred filename pattern is redwood_<artifact>_<YYYYMMDD> to make automated ingestion easier.
- Can you include an upload validation pass that returns a CSV with columns (object_key, md5, ingest_status, mapping_notes) so our pipeline can automatically reconcile?
- For CAIQ mapping: we’ll include both the CAIQ question id and a short human tag (e.g., CAIQ_1.5_aws_kms). If Vendr’s manifest validation flags missing mappings, please return row-level errors so we can correct before we re-upload.
- On the embargo: please do not expose files to any reviewers outside "Redwood Security Reviewers" until we flip release. We’ll provide the list of reviewer emails after upload.

Plan: we’ll prepare a compact bundle (~12 files) and the manifest today, attach here, and request presigns tomorrow AM. Can you confirm you’ll produce the upload-validation report after ingest?

If that’s all good I’ll send the manifest and target presign request tomorrow 08:00 PT.

Kimberly

On the schedule side, Marissa/Karthik — want to confirm our internal reviewer list (I’ve proposed marissa@redwood.com, security-ops@redwood.com) and that we can triage within 48 hours of upload. If yes I’ll proceed with the manifest creation.
